_doc: Inputs of RunnerBalance, the economy + power model behind the runner's 50-level curve (tests/Survival.Domain.Tests/RunnerBalanceTests.cs, docs/runner_balance.md). Hero stats, level-up gold / food / timers, star caps, shards, runner rewards, campaign stages, bounties, quests, the free gift pool, farm output and the rush rate are read from the real game files. Every number in THIS file is a modelling assumption; the ones marked _invented are placeholders Derek has to confirm (pace, village income, how often each profile buys). What a power pack holds and costs is read from stores.json (store.power_packs) and power_packs.json.

pace._invented: How a 'normal' free player plays: 3 sessions a day, each session tries the next runner level once (a beaten level can never be replayed, so there are no replays); the timeline stops after max_days.

village._invented: Free income outside the runner: farms (count and level assumed; output and capacity per level come from base_economy.json), how often the player collects them, how many of the 6 daily free gifts he opens, and the share of gold he puts into heroes (the rest goes on buildings: the model spends it on building and upgrading gold_mines Gold Mines, raising the Castle when a mine level needs it; mine output, cap, cost and timers per level come from base_economy.json buildable "mine", collected collections_per_day times like the farms). Campaign stages 1-6 and the bounties are assumed cleared one per day from day 1; the starter quests on day 1.

greedy._doc: Best power per cost: cost = gold + food_value * food.

profiles._invented: about $5 a week: the $1.99 starter once, then the $4.99 Knight's Satchel every week
about $20 a week: the starter once, then the $19.99 Warlord's Hoard every week
about $80 a week: the starter once, then the $39.99 King's Treasury twice a week
a free player who buys ONE $39.99 King's Treasury the first time he fails a level from L31 on (the free wall), and nothing else
